children: One of the most common plant species on

is the Chlovi, a large fungus that grows in large, spiraling patches all across the planet's surface. It is edible and, having become an important part of the local cuisine, is considered a delicacy. Attempts to cultivate Chlovi have varying degrees of success. Problems in the Chlovi's development arise when the fungi produce spores. Some growers hypothesize that Chlovi depends upon interaction with the predatory
, which use patches of the fungus as hunting and nesting grounds. The specific connection between the two is yet to be determined.
Chlovi grows in spiral formations, with individual plants consisting of oblong brown bodies with brightly colored phosphorescent red and orange gills that produce spores.
